en: In these aforementioned rituals, or in other activities as well,
one should offer a *bali* offering at the beginning and at the end for the sake of pacifying all obstacles.

In this regard, by this procedure: first of all, the preceptor, adorned with a crown and other ornaments as obtained, stands before the form of Śrī Vajrasattva. Having placed—in large vessels such as carts or baskets—food consisting of cooked rice, cakes, *yarpaṭa*, *laḍḍuka*, *jambuḍikā*, and so forth; fish, meat, rice, garlic, liquor, water, milk, and the like; accompanied by flowers and other offerings; decorated with canopies and the like; preceded by musical instruments; or whatever measure of food, drink, and so on is available—having thus arranged the various types of food to be chewed, eaten, licked, and drunk, [he proceeds] as before.

Having prepared the nectar (*amṛta*) according to the procedure for the accomplishment of nectar described in the *Gaṇacakra*, one should then—either by means of the *Piṇḍīkrama* procedure, the four-limbed procedure, the seed-syllables (*bīja*), and so forth, or instantaneously—worship all the Tathāgatas and others within the maṇḍala created with perfumes and other offerings before the form of Vajradhara as the Lord of one’s own wheel (*svacakreśa*). Having offered praise preceded by the ringing of the bell with the verses beginning "Akṣobhyavajra," and so forth:

Regarding this, the ritual procedure is as follows: first, the preceptor, adorned with a crown and other ornaments as obtained, stands before the glorious Vajrasattva; [he offers] into large vessels such as śāktas and pīṭhakas, food, flour-cakes, sugar, jambū fruits and the like, fish, meat, garlic, leeks, liquor, water, milk, and so forth.

Adorned with flowers, canopies, and the like, and arranged before musicians—or having properly set out even just food, water, and so forth as they are obtained—one should transform the foods, snacks, condiments, drinks, and so on into nectar through the ritual for accomplishing nectar (*amṛtasādhana*) as previously explained for the gaṇacakra.

Then, having performed a maṇḍala with fragrant substances and so forth before the form of Vajrasattva—whether through the ritual of the condensed sequence, the four-limbed ritual, from the seed-syllables and so forth, or even instantaneously—one should perfectly worship all the Tathāgatas, such as the Lord of one’s own wheel, and so on.
One should offer praise, preceded by the ringing of bells while reciting the verses beginning with "Akṣobhyavajra" and so forth.

With rays from the seed-syllable in one’s own heart, having drawn in Indra and the other gods with their retinues, the nāgas, and all sentient beings—[visualizing] the maṇḍala situated within the peaked pavilion at the center of the protective wheel of the ten wrathful deities—one should instantly contemplate Indra and the others as the deities of the assembly in union with their consorts. Then, preceded by the offering of water for the feet and so forth, while ringing the bell and brandishing the vajra, one should present the *bali* offering through the purification of the three spheres (*trimandala-viśuddhi*), with the firm resolve (*adhimokṣa*) that awakening mind (*bodhicitta*) is inseparable from emptiness and compassion.

Oṃ āḥ [Name]vajra! Having thus addressed each deity from the Lord of the Wheel down to Sumbha by their respective names and uttered their seed-syllables: "O destroyer of all wicked samayas and mudrās, grant me peace and protection, svāhā hūṃ!"

By means of the light rays from the seed-syllable at one’s own heart, the maṇḍala residing within the celestial palace situated at the hub of the ten-spoked protective wheel together with the wrathful deities, as well as Indra and his retinue, the nāgas, and all sentient beings, are summoned; then Indra and the others instantly enter into the state of clear light.

Having visualized the deities gathered in the retinue as being in the nature of wisdom (*prajñā*), one should ring the bell and brandish the vajra while preceded by the offering of water for the feet and so forth; then, with firm conviction in the bodhicitta—the indivisibility of emptiness and compassion—and through the complete purity of the three spheres, [one offers] the *bali* offerings.

oṃ āḥ hūṃ che ge mo vajra—thus reciting the names of each deity individually, from the lords of one’s own wheels (*cakreśvara*) down to Vighnāntaka, and pronouncing their seed-syllables as well: *sarvaduṣṭasamayamudrāprabhañjakamaśāntirakṣāṃ kuru svāhā hūṃ*.

Oṃ Āḥ! All the guardians of the world and all sentient beings throughout the infinite clouds and arrays of the world-systems of the ten directions and the three times—abiding in meditative absorption within the succession of mandalas of atoms that extend through the vast oceans of clouds of the infinite space of the ten directions of the three times; who have converged in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and reach to the limits of the expanse of space; who are equal to the sky-like extension of the infinite cloud-arrays of the world-systems of the ten directions and the three times—all you guardians of the world and all sentient beings, it is as follows:

Vajrāyudha, Māyāvajra, Vajrānala, Vajrakāla, Vajramusala, Nāgavajra, Vajrānila, Vajrabhairava, Vajraśauṇḍa, Vajrakrodha, Vajrakuṇḍali, Vajraprabha, Maunavajra, and Vemacitri—the Earth Deity—along with your retinues: please accept and enjoy this offering of bali consisting of flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, food offerings, and so forth, and [drive away] all obstructors and Vināyakas who steal my silver, gold, wealth, grain, longevity, youth, health, and true happiness.

Subdue, paralyze, bind, and destroy all wicked and malicious humans and non-humans! For the increase of my great happiness—my gold, silver, wealth, grain, longevity, youth, health, and true bliss—bring them forth until the end of the seat of enlightenment; provide true assistance, peace, and protection! HŪṂ!
oṃ sarvadhvajādaśadi-lokadhātvanantāgata-samudrameghavyūhaprasara-paramānuraja-maṇḍala-paramparānantargata-samāpattyavasthita-dharmadhātusamavasaraṇa-ākāśadhātuparyavasānaṃ sarvadhvajādaśadi |

O you who have come from the infinite world-realms! You who pervade the expanse of space! All world-protectors, for the sake of all sentient beings: namely, Vajrayudhamaya-vajra, Vajrānala-vajra, Vajrakāla-vajra, Musalanāga-vajra, Vajrānila-vajra, Vajrabhairava-vajra, Vajraśauṇḍa-vajra, Vajrakrodha-vajra, Kuṇḍalivajra, Prabhāvajra, and Vajravemacitrin!

Pṛthivīdevatāsaṃparivārāḥ | imaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ gandhaṃ naivedyam ādisaṃyuktabaliṃ upaharaṃ | pratīccha upabhujya | mama hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ dhanadhānyam āyuḥyauvanaṃ ārogyaṃ saukhyaṃ ca | praharakāṇa sarvavighnān vināśaya | sarvaduḥkhāni pradūḥkhāni |

ma nu śyā ma nu śyā | jambhaya stambhaya bandhaya vidhvamsaya | mamahi raṇya śūvarṇadhana dhānyādyupabandham | ārogyasatsukhāni | mahāsukhapravṛddhaye | yāvaddābodhimaṇḍaparyantaṃ dhaukayati sadā sahāyi kṣānti rakṣaṇya kuru hūṃ ||

Thus one should offer [the oblation] with these two mantras. Then, with the *nāgabali* mantra, one should mentally visualize those [deities] beginning with the lords of their respective maṇḍalas and ending with Sumbha, followed by Indra and the others together with their retinues, then the *nāgas*, and finally all sentient beings, as having tongues that are single-pronged vajras red in color at the syllable *hūṃ*. One should contemplate them consuming the nectar—drawn in by the rays of light from those [vajras]—as consisting of great bliss and having a single flavor with emptiness, for as long as desired.

One should also present [the offerings] with these mantras and the mantras of the *nāga*-bali. These [offerings] are made starting from the lord of one’s own maṇḍala down to Antaka (Gnod mdzes), followed by Indra and the other [deities] together with their retinues, and after them, the *nāgas*.

Then, one should visualize that all sentient beings have red, single-pointed vajras arising from the syllable *hūṃ* on their tongues; through these, nectar is drawn in by means of light rays or by the mind, and having been partaken of, it should be contemplated as being of the nature of great bliss, of one taste with emptiness, for as long as desired.

Having offered water for rinsing the mouth (*ācamana*), fragrant sandalwood paste, betel leaf (*tāmbūla*), and so forth, and having performed worship, one should ask those intent on accomplishing the task for forgiveness. Then, reciting the previously mentioned hundred-syllable mantra (*śatākṣaramantra*) and uttering, "Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through yoga; I am pure through yoga," while forming the *kamalāvarta* and *āliṅgana* mudrās, one should cause the circle of one's own deity (*svadevatācakra*) to enter into oneself. One should then establish the ten wrathful deities (*krodha*) residing in the protection-wheel (*rakṣācakra*) and Indra and the other guardians in the ten directions outside the mandala house, intent upon providing protection and accomplishing whatever is desired.

Having offered water for rinsing the mouth, fragrant sandalwood, betel nut, and so forth, and having performed the perfect worship, one should ask for forgiveness from those who have been primarily engaged in accomplishing the activities, and recite the previously explained hundred-syllable mantra: *oṃ yogaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ yogaśuddho ’ham*.

Having spoken thus, one performs the mudrās of the lotus circle and the embrace, and causes the mandala of one’s own deity to enter into oneself. Then, the ten wrathful deities residing in the protection wheel, along with Indra and the others who guard and are skilled in accomplishing desires, should be arrayed in the ten directions outside the pavilion of the maṇḍala.

From the commencement of the mandala rite until its conclusion—specifically after the dismissal of the powder mandala—one should perform the offering of bali and other rites, cause even the wrathful deities to enter into oneself, and then dismiss Indra and the others to their respective places while uttering three *cchoṭī*s.

This refers to the period from the commencement of the mandala rites until their final conclusion. Following the dismissal of the colored powder mandala, one should perform the offering of the *bali* and other rites; then, having caused the wrathful deities to enter into oneself and having snapped the fingers three times, one should request the Indras and other deities to depart to their respective abodes.
Furthermore, the daily offering of the *bali* at each junction of the day (*pratisandhya*) should be performed in this same manner.
Furthermore, the offering of bali to each individual sun is exactly like that.
This is the mantra for dismissal:
"The welfare of all sentient beings has been accomplished by you; success has been granted according to [your] capacity.
Go to the realm of the Buddhas, so that you may return again! Mur!"
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ. Because all phenomena are primordially unarisen, the letter A is the mouth [of all phenomena]; or [one may say] "hūṃ mur.
Or, reciting "oṃ āḥ hūṃ vajra mur," one should perform the dismissal.

This is the mantra for requesting departure: "Oṃ āḥ hūṃ akāro mukhaṃ sarvadharmāṇām ādy-anutpannatvāt hūṃ muḥ," or "Oṃ āḥ hūṃ vajra muḥ. By reciting this, one requests their departure. "You have accomplished all the welfare of sentient beings; please grant the corresponding attainments (siddhi). Even after departing for the realm of the Buddhas, please return once again."
In this context, one should understand the distinctions of time, direction, and color according to the primary differences in ritual activities such as pacification (*śānti*) and so forth.
One should understand the distinctions of time, direction, and color according to the primary differences in ritual activities such as pacification (*śānti*) and so forth.

Outside the maṇḍala house, in the directions starting from the east, one should cause offerings of food and so forth to be presented before the lumps of clay for the ten wrathful deities, using baskets, bowls, or cupped hands.

Outside the maṇḍala house, in the directions starting from the east, near the lumps of clay for the ten wrathful deities, one should offer food and so forth as bali-offerings, filling them in baskets, bowls, or cupped hands.
Outside of those clay balls, one should cause fifteen clay balls— or in their absence, mandalas—
to be offered upon [the ground] for the fifteen [deities] beginning with Indra in the eight directions.

On the left side of Indra is Viṣṇu with the illusory vajra; on his left side is Kuvera as Vajrabhairava. On the left side of that [Kuvera] is Vināyaka; [on his left] is Īśāna as Vajrakrodha. Between Īśāna and Upendra are Sūrya, Candra, and Brahmā. Between Varuṇa and Nairṛti are Vemacitrin and the Earth-deity. Thus, these fifteen banners, having their respective colors, belong to Indra and the others in their respective directions.
To the right of the sense-faculty (Indra) is Māyāvajra; Viṣṇu and Vajrabhairava are Virūpākṣa, and to his right is Vemacitrin.

Vajrakrodha is Īśāna; [he is located] between Īśāna and Upendra, amidst the sun, moon, and Brahmās, and between Varuṇa and Vidyutpati, upon Sthūṇakarṇa and the Earth Goddess (Pṛthivī). Thus, the fifteen banners of Indra and the others are in their respective directions.
Outside the clay balls of Indra and the others,
one should cause the nāgas to receive milk-bowls and so forth upon eight clay balls or upon circles made of cow dung.
Outside, one should scatter the sacrificial food (*balibhakta*) and so forth, as well as five streams— of ghee, honey, water,
liquor, and milk— clockwise.

Even when making an offering for another's sake, one should recite "me" or "my" exactly as it stands in the mantra according to the context, even if it is for someone else; furthermore, that person should be visualized as oneself. For through the intention—"In helping this very person, I am helping myself"—the accomplishment of that task occurs. And in the interim, one should make a request for their sake.

When offering the *bali* for the sake of others, one should recite the mantras exactly as they appear—using either "I" (*aham*), "me" (*mama*), or "my" (*mama*)—and one should maintain the firm conviction that [the recipient] is oneself. By benefiting this [recipient], one benefits oneself; thus, the meaning should be understood in the interim.
This is the ritual procedure for the universal *bali* of the assembly (*sāmājika*).
Thus concludes the ritual for the *bali* offering to all the spirits of the assembly.
"Converging into the realm of phenomena" (*dharmadhātusamavasaraṇā*) and so forth means that they have a single flavor with emptiness and culminate in emptiness.
"Dharmadhātusamavasaraṇā" means that they have a single taste with emptiness and compassion, and that they reach the ultimate limit of emptiness.

In this ritual of the bali offering, the offering made to the ten wrathful deities and others using the specific mantras taught in the tantras is exceedingly auspicious; however, those mantras have not been stated here for fear of prolixity.

Regarding the ritual of the *bali* offering, it is especially distinguished when the offerings for the ten wrathful deities (*daśakrodha*) are presented using their respective mantras as taught in their individual tantras; however, fearing that these mantras are too numerous, they have not been recited here.

Alternatively, one who possesses the yoga of the glorious *Saṃvara*, having prepared a maṇḍala with fragrant substances and the like, should worship his own wheel (*svacakra*) and praise it with the eight-line mantra. Then, by means of the rays of light from the syllable *HŪṂ* residing in his own heart, he should summon the maṇḍala situated within the peaked pavilion (*kūṭāgāra*) located at the center of the ten-spoked protection wheel (*rakṣācakra*) together with its wrathful deities; as well as Indra and the other guardians of the directions along with their retinues, and immeasurable sentient beings, from outside the protection wheel into the interior. Having formed the *jvālāmudrā* above his forehead, he should utter "Phet" three times with a majestic gesture and invoke the maṇḍala before him. [Regarding the *jvālāmudrā* and "pheḍ": (Note: The term *pheḍ* appears to be a transliteration of a Prakrit or Apabhraṃśa form related to the Sanskrit *phet*, a common seed-syllable used in tantric rituals for invocation.)

Furthermore, one who possesses the yoga of glorious Cakrasaṃvara should fashion a maṇḍala with fragrant substances and the like, perfectly worship his own wheel, and praise it with the eight-line mantra. Then, by means of the light rays from the syllable *hūṃ* residing in his own heart, he enters the celestial palace located at the hub of the ten-spoked protective wheel together with the wrathful deities.

Having summoned within the interior of the palace the maṇḍala and the outer regions outside the protection wheel (rakṣācakra), along with Indra and the others together with their retinues, as well as immeasurable sentient beings, one binds the blazing mudrā at the expanse of the forehead and, with a display of majesty, recites "pheṃ" three times while inviting the maṇḍala before oneself.

Oṃ kakka kahaṇa baddha bandhana khakkha khādana sarvaduṣṭānāṃ hana hana ghaggha ghātaya amukasya śāntiṃ kuru hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ jaḥ svāhā. Oṃ kakka kahaṇa bindha bandhana khakkha khādana sarvaduṣṭānāṃ hana hana ghaggha ghātaya amukasya śāntiṃ kuru hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ jaḥ svāhā.

Having thus invoked Indra and the other deities, and having instantly visualized them in the forms of the Saṃvara deities together with their consorts immediately after entering into emptiness, one should first offer water for the feet (*pādya*) and so forth. Then, as before, through the purification of the three spheres (*trimaṇḍala-viśuddhi*), one should place a vessel of nectar upon the *viśvavajra* at the center of the syllable *HŪṂ* situated on the moon within the palm of the left hand; having meditated thus, or else displaying that [vessel] with the index finger extended from the right hand formed into a vajra-fist, one should rotate it—circumambulating counter-clockwise in the cardinal directions according to the appropriate [deities], starting from the southeast corner and circling clockwise in the intermediate directions—for the Blessed One, his consort, the *ḍākinīs*, and the others such as Kākāsyā.

By means of this, having summoned the sense faculties and so forth, and having entered into emptiness through a single *saṃpūjā*, one should meditate on the form of the deity Cakrasaṃvara together with his consort. Preceded by the washing of the face and other rites, and as before, through the complete purity of the three spheres (*trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi*), [one should visualize] from the syllable *hūṃ* situated upon a moon disc in the palm of the left hand, the various [offerings].
Having arranged or visualized a vessel of nectar at the hub of the vajra, one displays it by extending the threatening gesture (*tarjanī*) from the right hand formed into a vajra-fist.

Then, for the Blessed One, his consort, the ḍākinīs, and so forth, as well as the owl-faced goddesses and others, one circumambulates counter-clockwise in the cardinal directions starting from the southeast corner, and clockwise in the intermediate directions.

Oṃ vajraḍāka imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa 2 hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ samayas tvaṃ dṛśya hoḥ. Having presented [the offering] by reciting this mantra one, two, three, four, or five times for the deities of the three wheels: Oṃ vajraḍāka imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ samayas tvaṃ dṛśya hoḥ.
Having offered by reciting this mantra once, twice, thrice, four times, and five times, [one offers] to the deities of the three wheels.

Oṃ, act! act! perform! perform! bind! bind! terrify! terrify! agitate! agitate! hrauṃ 2 hraḥ 2 pheṃ 2 phaṭ 2 burn! burn! cook! cook! devour! devour! O you who hang from a garland of entrails, blood, and fat, seize! seize! threaten the *bhujaṅgas* or serpents dwelling in the seven netherworlds! draw forth! draw forth! hrīṃ 2 jñauṃ 2 kṣmāṃ 2 hāṃ 2 hīṃ 2 hūṃ 2 kili 2 sili 2 hili 2 dhili 2 huṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!

Oṃ kara kara kuru kuru bandha bandha trāsaya trāsaya kro bhaya kṣobhaya hrīḥ hrīḥ hraḥ hraḥ phreṃ phreṃ phaṭ phaṭ daha daha pacaya pacaya bhakṣa bhakṣa vasarudhirāntamālavalambine gṛhṇa gṛhṇa saptapātālagatabhujaṅgān sarvaṃ bādhayata bādhayata ākaḍḍhya ākaḍḍhya hrīṃ hrīṃ jñauṃ.
With the mantra *dzNooM kSHmM kSHmM h'M h'M hiM hiM h'uM h'uM ki li ki li si li si li hi li hi li dhi li dhi li h'uM h'uM phaT sva h'a*, recited once, one should present the offering.
One should offer [the gift] by reciting this mantra once.
Thereafter, [one offers to] the ten wrathful deities residing on the spokes of the protection wheel.

Oṃ kha vajradhṛk vajrahūṃkāravajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajradaṇḍa vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajrānalārka vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajrakuṇḍali vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajrayakṣa vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajrakāla vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajramahābala vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajrabhīṣaṇa vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajroṣṇīṣacakravarti vajra hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ vajrapātāla vajra hūṃ phaṭ |

oṃ khaḥ vajra dhṛka vajra hūṃ kara vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra daṇḍa vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra ānālārka vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra kuṇḍali vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra yakṣa vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra kāla vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra mahābala vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajra bhīṣaṇa vajra hūṃ phaṭ |

*oṃ vajra auṣṇīṣacakravarti vajra hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ vajrapātāla vajra hūṃ phaṭ |* With these ten mantras, preceded by *hūṃ phaṭ*, one should interpose the formula: *“Take this bali! Take it! Grant peace to [Name] and provide protection!”* Reciting this once, one should offer [the bali] to the north, south, above, and below.

One should prefix each of these ten mantras with "aiṃ māṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa gṛhṇa amukasya śāntiṃ kuru rakṣāṃ kuru" before the syllables "hūṃ phaṭ," and by reciting them once each, one should offer them while circling to the left and right, as well as above and below.

Then, outside of that, for Indra and the others: Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi! May all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, unmādas, apasmāras, ḍākas, ḍākinīs, and so forth, accept this bali offering! Protect the pledge! Grant me all accomplishments! Eat, drink, smell, and enjoy as you please and according to your desire! Do not transgress! Be my companions for the sake of increasing my true happiness in every way! Hūṃ 2 phaṭ 2 svāhā!

oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi sarvadevanāgayakṣarākṣasabhūtapretapiśācaunmādāpasmāraḍākadākinīya imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇantu samaya rakṣantu | sarvasiddhiṃ me prayacchantu yatheṣṭam | yatheṣṭam | bhuñjatha pibatha jighratha mātikramatha ||
*Mā mā sarvākārtyāya tsukhaṃ vṛddhaye | sahāyikābhavantu hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!* By means of this,

having recited these two *āvarta* mantras four times each— once for the upward and once for the downward direction— one should present the offering. Thus, by reciting this four times, one should offer it while circling in both directions, above and below.
Regarding those [deities] beginning with the Lord of the Mandala and ending with Sumbha, the passage previously mentioned should also be understood here;
that is, from "those [deities] starting with the Lord of the Mandala and ending with Sumbha" onwards, as well as the other mantras, should be known.

But here, the hundred-syllable [mantra] is another: *Oṃ vajraheruka samayam anupālaya herukatvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava sutoṣyo me bhava anurakto me bhava supoṣyo me bhava sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha sarvakarmasu ca me cittaṃ śreyaḥ kuru hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ bhagavan vajraheruka mā me muñca heruko bhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ hūṃ phaṭ*.

oṃ vajraherukasamayamanupālaya | herukatvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava | sutoṣyo me bhava | anurakto me bhava | supoṣyo me bhava | sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha sarvakarmasu ca me cittaṃ śreyah kuru hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ bhagavān vajraheruka mā me muñca herukabhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā ||

Regarding the colors, arms, and other attributes of the ten wrathful deities mentioned here as described in the *Abhidhānottara*, they should be understood in brief from the previously mentioned *Śrīsaṃvara* maṇḍala.
% *Abhidhānottara*!

% Here, the body colors, hand symbols, and so forth of the ten wrathful deities (*krodha*) taught as the supreme *abhidhāna* should be understood as being correctly summarized within the previously mentioned maṇḍala of Śrī Saṃvara.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the bali offering to all spirits according to the vows.
This is the *bali* offering for all spirits (*sarvabhūta*) of Saṃvara.

Alternatively, one who has the form of Śrī Hevajra, by means of the rays from the *hūṃ* syllable residing in the heart, draws forth Indra and the other [deities] together with their retinues, as well as immeasurable sentient beings, from the directions outside the protection wheel of the maṇḍala—which is situated within the peaked pavilion (*kūṭāgāra*) inside the ten-armed wrathful protection circle. for the sake of securing well-being, one should offer—according to what is available and according to one's ability—the collection of materials consisting of curd, milk, ghee, honey, sugar, non-meat side dishes, fragrant water, scented garlands for the head, loose flowers, white sandalwood and other fragrant substances, as well as incense such as agarwood, guggulu, and the ten-ingredient blend, along with lamps and so forth.

For the pacification of obstacles such as those arising from cities and so forth, one should prepare large vessels such as carts; this is the detailed procedure. Adorned with a crown and other ornaments as obtained, his mind permeated by compassion and loving-kindness, having knelt upon the earth with his right knee and joined his palms in *añjali*, facing either east or north, he should recite these verses for the worship of the planets in one place.

With flowers, perfumes, garlands, incense, And offerings of bali and radiant lamps, I respectfully present these; Having accepted them, please partake and drink, And may you likewise be endowed with the fruits of this activity.

This is the fourfold offering (*bali*) in the generation stage (*utpattikrama*). In the completion stage (*utpannakrama*), however, it is the presentation of an offering of *bali*—which is non-different from the essence of gnosis—to Indra and the other deities, together with the deity who is the Lord of one’s own chosen maṇḍala, [all of whom] appear solely through the mere mental visualization by means of a mind that has not moved away from wisdom (*prajñā*) and method (*upāya*).

These four *bali* offerings pertain to the stage of generation (*utpattikrama*). Regarding the stage of completion (*niṣpannakrama*), with a mind unwavering from wisdom (*prajñā*) and method (*upāya*), one simply offers the *bali*—which is inseparable from the flavor of primordial wisdom (*jñānāmṛta*)—to the deities such as the Lord of the Desired Maṇḍala and the Indras and others who have been invited through mere mental intention, [the deities] whose very nature is wisdom and method.
